overview: PPE (Positional Preservation Embedding) is a parameter-free, plug-and-play positional encoding strategy that preserves spatiotemporal layout during visual token compression in MLLMs by splitting embedding dimensions to encode multiple position IDs per merged token, and supports cascade clustering for progressive multi-layer compression.

modules.name: M-RoPE Positional Encoding Module
modules.description: Implement the Multi-dimensional Rotary Position Embedding (M-RoPE) as the foundation, which partitions embedding dimensions into sections for temporal, height, and width axes, supporting both 2D (image) and 3D (video) positional ID assignment according to configurable section sizes.

modules.name: PPE Core Operator
modules.description: Implement the Positional Preservation Embedding operator that, given a merged token cluster, selects top-K position IDs (by distance to cluster center), splits each embedding dimension into K equal chunks, and assigns different position IDs to different chunks so that a single compressed token simultaneously encodes multiple original positions via the RoPE rotation mechanism.

modules.name: DPC-KNN Token Clustering
modules.description: Implement the Density Peak Clustering with KNN algorithm for visual token merging, computing token similarity, identifying cluster centers, and producing cluster group assignments where tokens within each group are averaged to form compressed token embeddings.

modules.name: Top-K Position ID Selection
modules.description: Implement the position ID selection strategy for PPE: for each cluster group, rank constituent tokens by their distance to the cluster center, select the top-K position IDs, and handle cases where cluster size is smaller than K by repeating high-weight tokens to fill slots.

modules.name: Cascade Compression Pipeline
modules.description: Implement the multi-layer cascade compression pipeline that applies token clustering with PPE at multiple transformer layers (e.g., layers 11, 23, 35), progressively merging tokens and updating PPE position IDs across stages, ensuring that the number of preserved position IDs reduces gradually during repeated merges.

modules.name: Visual Token Preprocessing
modules.description: Implement visual input preprocessing for Qwen2.5-VL, including dynamic resolution handling (min/max pixel constraints for images and videos), frame sampling for video inputs (maximum frame limit), and patch tokenization that produces the initial set of visual token embeddings with their 3D position IDs.

modules.name: SFT Dataset Construction
modules.description: Implement the supervised fine-tuning dataset construction pipeline that curates image and video instruction-tuning samples from LLaVA-Video-178k and LLaVA-OneVision, with even down-sampling, separate configurations for image (approx 300K) and video (approx 120K) training sets.

modules.name: MLLM Integration Wrapper
modules.description: Implement the integration layer that plugs PPE-based compression into the Qwen2.5-VL model pipeline, replacing or augmenting the default visual token flow between the vision encoder and the LLM backbone, and optionally inserting compression modules within specified LLM transformer layers.

modules.name: Training Loop with Differential Learning Rates
modules.description: Implement the supervised fine-tuning loop with gradient accumulation, separate learning rates for the visual encoder, patch merger, and LLM backbone, learning rate warmup, and single-epoch training schedule with all parameters unfrozen.

modules.name: Multi-Benchmark Evaluation Suite
modules.description: Implement evaluation runners for all benchmarks used in the paper: MMBench (EN/CN) for general visual understanding, TextVQA/DocVQA/OCRBench/ChartQA for layout and document understanding, VideoMME/NeXT-QA/SEED-Bench-Video/MVBench for temporal understanding, each following their respective evaluation criteria and metric computation.

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Implement the ablation study framework covering: (1) effect of K (number of preserved position IDs per cluster), (2) effect of reduction ratios (25%–90%), (3) single-stage vs. multi-stage aggregation, (4) before-LLM vs. within-LLM compression, (5) spatial-only vs. spatiotemporal compression, and (6) ID retention ratio computation.

modules.name: Cross-Method Compatibility Integration
modules.description: Implement PPE integration adapters for multiple baseline compression methods (ChatUniVi, PACT, ToMe, VisionZip), demonstrating plug-and-play compatibility in both training-free and SFT settings, ensuring PPE's position ID redistribution works with each method's token selection and aggregation mechanisms.

modules.name: Attention Visualization and Statistics
modules.description: Implement attention map extraction from specified LLM layers, projection of text-visual attention weights back onto original images as heatmaps, and computation of entropy and variance statistics for quantitative comparison of attention sharpness and confidence between compression methods.

modules.name: Computational Efficiency Analysis
modules.description: Implement profiling for inference time (LLM generation time), peak GPU memory usage, and token reduction ratio measurement across different compression configurations, enabling comparison of efficiency-accuracy trade-offs.

modules.name: Experiment Configuration and Result Aggregation
modules.description: Implement configuration management for all experiment variants (model sizes, compression settings, benchmark selections), logging integration, checkpoint management, and automated result aggregation producing comparison tables (dense vs. compressed, with/without PPE, across all benchmarks).
